## ppwr-chase-scheduler

The part that makes a campaign finish.

Most of a campaign is waiting. Suppliers do not answer first time, and what separates one that closes from one that rots is whether anybody follows up on a schedule instead of when they happen to remember.

**Reminders are counted from the invitation**, not from the last reminder. Skip a run for a week and the reminder that fell due in the meantime goes out, instead of every later one sliding a week back.

**Never more than the campaign asked for.** `reminder_days` is the whole schedule, so a supplier on a three step campaign gets nudged three times and is then left alone.

**One message per supplier**, not one per item. Forty open items is one email, the same way the invitation was.

**Expiry is a state change, not a delete.** Past the campaign's expiry the item moves to `expired`, the owner is told, and everything collected against it stays where it is.

**The decision is a plain function of the rows and the date**, tested outside n8n. A scheduler you can only prove by running it for three weeks is one no one trusts.

Code nodes are built from `src/` by `npm run bundle`.

### Look

Every campaign, every open item, and who to write to. No writes on this lane.

### Chase and expire

Nudge the ones that are due, close the ones that are out of time.

nodes.name: Every morning
nodes.notes: Daily. The schedule lives on the campaign, not here, so changing when a supplier is chased is a data change instead of a workflow edit.

nodes.name: Defaults
nodes.notes: Notices are off out of the box. A scheduler that starts mailing a real supplier list the moment it is deployed is a scheduler that gets switched off again.

nodes.name: Load settings
nodes.notes:
Soft. No meta rows means the defaults stand.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.notes:
Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

The same settings 03 and 06 run on, read the same way.

nodes.name: Load campaigns
nodes.notes:
Loaded once and matched in memory. A daily run over a few hundred items would otherwise make a few hundred identical reads.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Load items for chase
nodes.notes:
Only to find out who owns each item. The message goes to the vendor, not to the SKU.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Load open items
nodes.notes:
The four states a supplier can still act from. Anything conform, closed, withdrawn, expired or in error is somebody else's problem.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.notes:

Every open item sorted into chase today, give up on, or leave alone.

value.transition: ={{ { campaign_item_id: $json.campaign_item_id, from_state: $json.state, to_state: 'expired', event_type: 'expired', actor: 'system', payload: { days_since_invite: $json.days_since_invite, reminders_sent: $json.reminder_count } } }}

nodes.name: Expire item
nodes.notes:
Expired is a state, not a deletion. Everything collected against the item stays where it is, and the event log says when we stopped waiting.

Mode is 'each'.

nodes.name: Build reminders
nodes.notes:
Built from src/. Rebuild with npm run bundle.

Grouped by supplier, so forty open items are one message instead of forty.

nodes.name: Send reminders?
nodes.notes: Nothing is marked as reminded unless a reminder actually went out. A run with notices off leaves the counters exactly where they were, so switching them on later chases from the right place instead of from the beginning.

nodes.name: Mark reminded
nodes.notes:
The counter is set to the reminder number that just went out, not incremented, so a run that partly failed and was repeated does not skip a step.

Mode is 'each'.
